full_judgment:
Chowdhury A.T.M. Masud, J:- This appeal by special leave is directed against the order dated 6:12.190 passed by the High Court Division, Rangpur Bench, in Criminal Revision No. 103 of 1983, refusing to quash the proceeding against the appellants in C.R. case No. 763, of 1983 pending in the Court of Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Rangpur. 

 3. The learned Magistrate after examining the complainant on oath took cognizance of the alleged offence and issued warrant of arrest, against the accused appellants, under section 193/197/199/420/109 of the Penal Code. The appellants voluntarly surrendered and were granted bail by the Sessions Judge, Rangpur, in .criminal, Miscellaneous Case No. 80(3) of 1983. The appellants thereafter moved the High Court Division, Rangpur Bench, under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, for quashing the said criminal proceeding against them and obtained a rule which was ultimately discharged by a Division Bench of the High Court Division, Rangpur Bench. 

 5. Mr. B.N. Chowdhury, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellants argues that even assuming that the allegations against the appellants are true no criminal prosecution can be maintained against them so long the decree even though ex-parte is, is not challenged and set aside by an appropriate forum. He further argues that in view of the provision of section 476, read with section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Magistrate was not competent to take cognizance, either under section 193 or section 199 of the Penal Code without a complaint from the Court concerned and that no prima facie case under section 197 or 420/109 has been disclosed in the complaint petition. 

 10. Having gone through the petition of complaint and other relevant materials, we are unable to accept this contention. The petition of complaint does not disclose any offence against the appellants, either under section 197 or under section 420/109 of the Penal Code. Moreover so long the decree passed by the Civil Court remains in force, it is a good defence for the appellants in criminal prosecution. No useful purpose will be served by further continuation of the criminal proceeding. The learned Judges of the High Court Division did not apply their minds to this aspect of the case and as such they are not justified in refusing to quash the proceeding. 

 11. For the aforesaid reasons the judgment of the High Court Division is set aside and C.R. Case No. 763 of 1983 pending in the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Rangpur, is quashed. The appeal is allowed.
